terms.comment: Our phrase, with the ancient adjective holitōrius, of vegetables, as in the forum holitōrium, the vegetable market of Rome (Varro, Livy, in Lewis & Short s.v. olitōrius). Mēnsa is the classical word for the table goods are sold from (Lewis & Short: “a market-stand for meat, vegetables, etc.”), as in the fruit stall, mēnsa pōmāria. Morgan–Owens has a taberna, a booth, for a produce stand.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. produce stand, fruit stand.
Lewis & Short: mensa · Lewis & Short: olitorius
